stories.headline: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeats Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th Congressional District
stories.summary:
Retired Navy rear admiral Eileen Laubacher, a Democrat, has defeated Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's 4th Congressional District, according to a race call by The Associated Press. The result came after more than a week of vote counting following the Nov. 3 election. The district includes the Eastern Plains and Douglas County.

Boebert had sought a fourth term in the House. She moved to the more conservative 4th District after a close re-election contest in 2022. Her loss flips a seat that has traditionally favored Republicans.

A Colorado Sun analysis found that Boebert's defeat makes her one of the worst-performing incumbent Republican House members in the midterms, relative to how President Donald Trump fared in 2024. The outcome shows how far Democrats made inroads in conservative-leaning territory this year.

The result is part of a broader Democratic showing in Colorado, where the party is on track to flip three Republican-held congressional seats and hold seven of the state's eight House seats.

stories.headline: Medical examiner rules Denver in-custody death of Milton Banks a homicide
stories.summary:
The Denver Office of the Medical Examiner has ruled the death of Milton Banks, 42, a homicide nearly four months after he died following a struggle with Denver police officers. The office concluded he died of cardiopulmonary arrest following a prolonged struggle with law enforcement and physical restraint. A homicide ruling does not by itself establish criminal culpability.

Police said the encounter began with 911 calls around 4:22 p.m. on July 14 reporting a fight in the 2100 block of East Colfax Avenue. One caller said a man in underwear tried to carjack a vehicle and was struck by an occupant. Officers handcuffed Banks, and police said a preliminary investigation found they did not use a Taser or pepper spray. He was taken by ambulance to St. Joseph Hospital, where he died. The medical examiner reported synthetic cannabinoids in his system.

The Denver Police Department opened an investigation with the Colorado State Patrol, the Colorado Bureau of Investigation and the Denver District Attorney's Office, overseen by the Office of the Independent Monitor. It remains unclear why the ruling took nearly four months. Between 2020 and 2024, 348 people died in custody in Colorado, according to Justice Department data.

stories.headline: Barry Morphew pleads guilty to careless driving in Denver hit-and-run case
stories.summary:
Barry Morphew, who faces a murder charge in the death of his wife Suzanne, pleaded guilty Friday to careless driving in a separate hit-and-run case. Under the plea deal, four other charges were dropped. He will serve 60 days in jail, and restitution will be decided later.

Authorities said the crash occurred in Denver on Aug. 26, when Morphew allegedly drove aggressively and hit two vehicles. Video showed him trying to buff scratches off a car and refusing to identify himself. Officials said he offered the other driver $300, which she declined, then left after learning authorities had been called. He was arrested Sept. 3.

Prosecutors reviewed GPS data from a monitor Morphew was wearing, and a judge then imposed stricter home restrictions with no exceptions. Suzanne Morphew vanished in Chaffee County six years ago, and her remains were found in 2023. Morphew was arrested in Arizona in 2025 in connection with her death and is scheduled to go on trial in July 2027.

stories.headline: Nationwide FAA ground stop disrupts flights at Denver International Airport
stories.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop Friday because of widespread communications problems, causing hundreds of flights to be delayed or canceled at Denver International Airport. The FAA halted takeoffs and began bringing planes out of the sky around 2 p.m.

Departures at the airport faced a roughly six-hour gap, with the last flight leaving at 1:38 p.m. before the stop. Denver was among the airports that received diverted flights, along with Chicago O'Hare, Dallas Fort Worth and Reagan National. Colorado Springs Airport said it was ready to accept diversions if needed.

Flights resumed after the stop was lifted, but U.S. airlines warned that disruptions could continue well beyond the order. Some travelers at DIA faced consequences including a missed funeral and a basketball tournament a team may not reach.

stories.headline: Denver Health buys remaining Bannock Street parcel for $1.2 million
stories.summary:
Denver Health has purchased property adjacent to its main campus as the city's safety-net hospital plans future expansion. The hospital bought the remaining portion of the 567 N. Bannock St. parcel for $1.2 million this month, according to city records.

The purchase adds to land next to the hospital's central campus near downtown Denver. The records do not detail specific plans for the site, but the acquisition is tied to the hospital's longer-term growth.

Denver Health serves as the city's main safety-net provider, caring for a large share of uninsured and Medicaid patients in the metro area.

stories.headline: Deadly motorcycle crash closes southbound I-25 in Lone Tree
stories.summary:
A deadly motorcycle crash shut down parts of Interstate 25 near Lone Tree overnight Friday, according to the City of Lone Tree. At 12:47 a.m., the Colorado State Patrol said southbound I-25 near milepost 195 was closed.

Law enforcement officers investigated the scene. Immediate details about the victim, the cause of the crash and the number of vehicles involved were not available.

The closure forced southbound traffic off the highway while crews worked at the scene. Drivers were advised to seek alternate routes during the investigation.

stories.headline: Colorado Democratic Party chair says 'blue wave' oversimplifies election results
stories.summary:
Shad Murib, chair of the Colorado Democratic Party, said describing the midterm results as a blue wave is an oversimplification. He said voters were responding to rising costs of living and rejecting Republican policies, in contrast with the vision Democrats offered.

Colorado Democrats are on track to flip three Republican-held congressional seats, giving the party seven of the state's eight House seats. Murib said it was the first time every Republican-held congressional seat was on both the state and national party maps. He also cited wins at the local level, including in Eagle and Grand counties.

Murib pointed to organizers in Douglas and El Paso counties who worked to flip county seats. He said Democrats must now deliver, arguing that a big win is not political capital to save but to spend on behalf of voters, and that the work ahead will include Republicans.

stories.headline: Push for new leadership overshadows Democratic celebration at Denver conference
stories.summary:
Division over who should lead congressional Democrats in January 2027 was on display at the two-day What's Next conference in Denver, held to celebrate the party's election gains. Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland announced Thursday evening that he is challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, saying the party needs new leadership.

Van Hollen, who ruled out a 2028 presidential bid, called himself the underdog but said many colleagues want a different approach. Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan said she is not voting for Schumer and would say more next week. Schumer was not scheduled to appear in Denver.

Protesters from the Sunrise Movement repeatedly disrupted House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries during his first onstage appearance. Jeffries, expected to become speaker in January, faces no challenger, though some incoming freshmen aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America have not committed to supporting him.

stories.headline: Avalanche give update on MacKinnon and Makar after lower-body injuries
stories.summary:
Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar offered the first update on Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar after both left Thursday's 4-3 overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators with lower-body injuries. Both were hurt in the second period at Canadian Tire Centre.

Shane Pinto scored his second goal of the night 2:08 into overtime to give Ottawa the win. The Avalanche have since made a roster move that may signal concern about MacKinnon's availability.

Colorado is next scheduled to face the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday night. MacKinnon's chances of playing in that game remain uncertain.

stories.headline: Rockies unlikely to rush a Hunter Goodman trade despite rumors
stories.summary:
As MLB general manager meetings wrapped up in Las Vegas, insider Jon Morosi reported that rival teams believe the Rockies are more willing to trade All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman than they were at the deadline. Goodman, 27, hit 41 home runs last season and is under team control through 2029.

General manager Josh Byrnes said any extension is on hold until the Rockies understand the financial implications of a new collective bargaining agreement. Paul DePodesta said position players are a strength and will be harder to trade, though the club must be open-minded.

The Rockies must rebuild their rotation, with only two healthy starters under contract and ready for a full season. Any Goodman deal would likely require major league-ready pitching in return, a high price for suitors.

stories.headline: Nuggets send Nembhard and Whitmore to G League as team sits at 6-4
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets assigned two-way players Cam Whitmore and Nembhard to the Grand Rapids Gold, their G League affiliate, to get regular playing time. Both remain available for call-ups as depth.

Denver is 6-4 to start the season in a Western Conference deeper than expected. Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray have done much of the work, while the Nuggets also welcomed Spencer Jones back to the lineup.

Trade speculation continues around Aaron Gordon and Cam Johnson, though a ClutchPoints report said Denver is not necessarily shopping either player.

topStory.headline: Bomb Found at Peoria Ethanol Plant Prompts One-Mile Evacuation in Illinois; Device Rendered Safe, Search Continues
topStory.summary:
Authorities in Peoria, Illinois, evacuated a one-mile radius around the BioUrja Renewables ethanol plant on Friday after a suspicious package was found at the facility. The evacuation covered commercial and residential areas on both sides of the Illinois River, in Peoria and neighboring East Peoria. Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said the plant received a bomb threat Friday, and a suspicious package was located around 2 p.m. Several hours later, officials deemed it a credible threat and set the blast radius at one mile. Bomb technicians rendered the device safe later that night.

Dixon said early Saturday that the area had not been declared safe and that the evacuation order remained in effect. He said the entire property would have to be searched, a process expected to last several hours, and he declined to say how many devices had been found, where they were located, or whether there were suspects. Mayor Rita Ali said Friday night, "A device has been identified. We know it's a credible threat. We know it's a bomb," and added that officials did not know whether there was one device or several. She said the search began after "electronic communication that there was a bomb," and that it was paused overnight because of darkness, with crews due to resume around sunrise.

FBI Special Agent Ryan Presley said FBI personnel, along with local and state police, determined the suspicious package was a threat and rendered it safe. Agents from the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives were also at the scene, and Illinois state troopers blocked traffic in the area. Interstate 74 was closed in both directions through Peoria, and Peoria County Sheriff Chris Watkins advised drivers to use Interstate 474 to bypass the city. Gov. JB Pritzker, Rep. Darin LaHood and Rep. Eric Sorensen urged residents to follow evacuation orders, and Sorensen met with evacuees at Peoria Emanuel High School, the designated shelter. Ali urged residents without transportation to call 911 or the local Red Cross chapter.

The disruption extended beyond the evacuation zone. Country singer Jon Pardi canceled his Friday concert at the Peoria Civic Center at the direction of the police chief, and Dozer Park, home of the Peoria Chiefs minor league baseball team, canceled a holiday event. OSF HealthCare St. Francis Medical Center, located nearby, said it was taking appropriate precautions and monitoring the situation. It was not immediately clear how many people lived within the evacuation zone in Peoria, a city of about 110,000 residents.

BioUrja Renewables operates the former ADM ethanol plant in Peoria, which produces beverage-grade and industrial alcohol. Its parent, BioUrja Group, runs 19 other plants in the United States and has facilities in Mexico, Singapore, India, the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom. Attempts by the New York Times to reach BioUrja officials were not immediately successful. City officials said they would provide an update by 9 a.m. and more information around midday Saturday, with the evacuation to remain in place until the facility search is complete and the area is declared safe.
